# SPEC 4.0.2 — Window Names, Preview & Layout Fixes (v002) {.unnumbered}

| | |
|---|---|
| **Software version** | 4.0.2 |
| **Spec revision** | v002 (supersedes v001) |
| **Date** | 2026-07-22 |
| **Status** | Implemented |

This revision extends v001 (sequential window names) with three further
issues reported against the same release, plus a source-tree reconciliation
that investigation of those issues uncovered.

## Issue 1 — Sequential default window names

Unchanged from v001: default window names are `window1`, `window2`, … in
window order instead of adjective/noun pairs ("Able Ant", "Blue Bear").
`services/nameGenerator.ts` shrank from ~97 lines to 18; custom names and AI
"Auto Name" results still override defaults. See v001 for full details.

## Issue 2 — Right-hand side breaks when resizing the browser window

**Problem.** Shrinking the browser window sometimes clipped or garbled the
right side of the layout (tab table columns disappearing under the preview
pane, pane pushed off-screen).

**Cause.** Two compounding flex-layout defects:

- The tab table uses `whitespace-nowrap`, giving `<main>` a large intrinsic
  width. `<main>` had no `min-width: 0`, and a flex item's default
  `min-width: auto` prevents it from shrinking below its content — so the row
  overflowed its `overflow-hidden` container.
- The preview pane has a fixed pixel width (250–800 px, `shrink-0`) that was
  only clamped during drag-resize, never against the viewport. On a small
  window the pane could claim more room than exists.

**Fix** (`App.tsx`):

- `min-w-0` added to `<main>` so it shrinks properly (its content scrolls
  within it instead of overflowing the row).
- The preview pane gets `max-width: 70vw`, and the drag-resize clamp now also
  caps at 70% of the viewport width.

## Issue 3 — Preview pane hidden by default

**Problem.** The preview pane started hidden; users had to find the eye
toggle in the toolbar to enable it.

**Fix.** `showPreview` initial state changed from `false` to `true` in
`App.tsx`. The toolbar eye toggle and the pane's close button still hide it.

## Issue 4 — Some tabs show "Preview Unavailable"; wake-up support

**Why previews fail.** The content preview injects a script into the target
tab (`chrome.scripting.executeScript`) and renders the captured HTML in a
sandboxed iframe. Capture fails for:

1. **Discarded ("sleeping") tabs** — Chrome's Memory Saver unloads tabs not
   visited recently; there is no page to script. This is per-tab, not
   per-window, which made the failures look random across windows.
2. **Restricted pages** — `chrome://` pages, the Chrome Web Store, other
   extensions' pages. Browser policy; not fixable.

**New behavior.** When capture fails and `chrome.tabs.get(...).discarded` is
true, the error panel explains the tab is asleep and offers a
**"Wake up & preview"** button. Clicking it:

1. Calls `chrome.tabs.reload(tabId)` — reloads the tab in the background
   without stealing focus from the dashboard.
2. Waits for the tab's `onUpdated` event to report `status: 'complete'`
   (15 s timeout).
3. Retries the content capture automatically.

An explicit button was chosen over auto-waking on click: waking a tab spends
the memory/network Chrome was saving and can re-trigger session refreshes, so
the user stays in control. Restricted pages keep the existing explanation and
"Go to Tab" fallback.

## Source-tree reconciliation

Investigating issue 4 revealed that the installed extension was built from
`~/Downloads/tabmaster10`, a divergent copy containing the content-preview
feature (`getTabContent`, iframe preview panel, `scripting` permission) that
this repository lacked. That feature has now been merged into this repo,
which is again the single source of truth:

- `services/tabService.ts` — `getTabContent` copied in; new `isTabDiscarded`
  and `wakeTab` helpers added.
- `components/PreviewPanel.tsx` — replaced with the content-preview version,
  extended with the sleeping-tab detection and wake-up flow.
- `manifest.json` — `scripting` permission added.

## Affected files

- `App.tsx` — preview default on; `min-w-0` on `<main>`; viewport clamps on
  the preview pane width.
- `components/PreviewPanel.tsx` — content preview + wake-up flow.
- `services/tabService.ts` — `getTabContent`, `isTabDiscarded`, `wakeTab`.
- `services/nameGenerator.ts` — (from v001) sequential names.
- `manifest.json` — `scripting` permission.

## Out of scope

- Persisting the preview pane's visibility/width across sessions.
- Bulk-waking all tabs in a window.
- Any preview for restricted pages.
